To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the explicit asymptotic expansion of the two-loop diagram in the Sudakov (or high-energy) limit can be obtained by summing up all the terms of the expansion over a specific family (subgraph) of the original diagram.

(i) the algorithm for analytical calculation is based on a new method of asymptotic expansions of two loop diagrams in the Sudakow limit (ii) it is applicable to typical diagrams with two non-zero external momenta and two non-zero masses (iii) it is based on a specific family of the subgraphs of a diagram and (iv) the interplay of the divergences is the key feature of the new algorithm.

(i) the algorithm is applicable to any Feynman diagram; (ii) it is based on a sum over subgraphs; (iii) it provides the leading and next-to-leading terms in the asymptotic expansion; (iv) it involves all the three types of divergences, ultraviolet, colliner and infrared, which cancel each other in the sum; (v) the algorithm is based on a simple and transparent formula which is valid for any Feynman graph.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the problem of the analytical calculation of Feynman integrals with two non-zero scales in the asymptotic limit of one of them, which has been solved in a number of papers for the case of the off-shell limit.
the development and application of a new approach to asymptotic expansions of multi-loop Feynman integrals.
the problem of calculation of Feynman integrals in the Sudakov region, i.e. when all the external momenta are of the order of Q, and all the masses are small compared to Q.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these explicit asymptotic formulae are very useful for practical applications.
the explicit formulae for the coefficients c nj, n = 0, j = 0,…,4, in the asymptotic expansions of two loop diagrams with one non-zero and two non-zero masses have been derived.
the asymptotic expansion for the two-loop diagram with one mass, as well as the leading terms for the case of two masses, are obtained in a completely analytic form.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to calculate analytically the leading terms in the asymptotic expansion of two-loop diagrams in the Sudakow limit.

we have developed a method for the analytical calculation of asymptotic expansions of two-particle irreducible Feynman diagrams for any number of loops in the Sudakov regime, i.e. for large values of the ratio of the external momentum squared to the masses of the particles running in the loop.
we have developed an efficient method to obtain all powers in the asymptotic expansion of a two-loop diagram with non-zero masses in the Sudakov region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the method of asymptotic expansion is a powerful tool for analytical evaluation of Feynman diagram coefficients in the Sudakov region.
the method is applicable in the case of two-loop diagrams with two non-zero external masses, and that the results are in good agreement with the existing ones obtained by other methods.
the asymptotic expansions of the diagrams with non-zero masses can be calculated analytically.
